title: Streaming SSE chunking/backpressure debug notes - repro
content:
Summary:
- Intermittent stalls / client-side hang when streaming long SSE responses from the runtime (hosted API + dedicated). Usually after ~40-100KB of payload. Connection often stays open but no further events are delivered, or we see a sudden socket close (EPIPE) from upstream.

Observed behavior (examples):
- curl -v -N gets initial events, then stops receiving further chunks; connection still open.
- Browser clients (EventSource / fetch + ReadableStream) show no more data, client-side backpressure not triggered.
- Server logs show writer.flush success, no errors for a while, then eventually a 502/504 from proxy or EPIPE.
- Repro is 80% on instances behind ALB/NGINX with default buffering; rare on direct node -> runtime local test.

Repro steps (minimal):
1) Start a small HTTP SSE endpoint (example python below) that emits 1KB chunk every 50ms for 1000 chunks.
2) Put nginx reverse proxy with default proxy_buffering ON between client and endpoint OR route through our ALB.
3) curl -v -N http://<proxy>/sse-test and observe stall after ~60KB.

Minimal SSE server (python, for repro):
# sse_test.py (uvicorn + fastapi)
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()

async def event_stream():
    for i in range(1000):
        chunk = f"data: chunk-{i}\n\n".encode()
        yield chunk
        await asyncio.sleep(0.05)

@app.get('/sse-test')
async def sse_test():
    return StreamingResponse(event_stream(), media_type='text/event-stream')

Run: uvicorn sse_test:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000

Commands tried (client side):
- curl -v -N http://host/sse-test  # -N to disable buffering on curl
- curl -v --no-buffer http://host/sse-test
- node fetch + stream reader (ReadableStream) to test backpressure
- eventsource polyfill in browser (same behavior)

Server-side experiments:
- Increased flush frequency (flushed per chunk) - no change behind proxy.
- Switched content-length/chunked encoding explicitly - still stalls.
- Disabled gzip compression (proxy and app) - no change.
- Set response headers: Connection: keep-alive, Cache-Control: no-transform

Proxy experiments:
- nginx: set proxy_buffering off; proxy_request_buffering off; chunked_transfer_encoding on -> fixes in local repro consistently.
- ALB: observed the stall still happens; ALB likely buffers up to a threshold. No easy ALB config to fully disable buffering.

Error snippets / logs (truncated):
- Client curl verbose:
  * Connected to proxy (10.0.0.5) port 80 (#0)
  > GET /sse-test HTTP/1.1
  < HTTP/1.1 200 OK
  data: chunk-0
  data: chunk-1
  ...
  (after ~70KB)
  * read error: Connection reset by peer
  * Closing connection 0

- Server log (runtime):
  2024-11-03T15:12:21.123Z INFO writer flushed chunk-63 (size=1024)
  2024-11-03T15:12:21.176Z INFO writer flushed chunk-64 (size=1024)
  2024-11-03T15:12:23.001Z WARN write EPIPE when writing chunk-67
  2024-11-03T15:12:23.002Z ERROR connection closed by client

Hypotheses:
- Proxy buffering thresholds (nginx default proxy_buffers/proxy_buffer_size) cause proxy to buffer a few chunks then either stall or drop connection once internal thresholds are crossed. nginx off = works -> strong signal.
- ALB/Cloud LB likely buffers too (Layer7) and closes/halts streaming once internal limit reached. Might need chunked responses with flush/transfer-encoding trick and keep-alive proper headers.
- TLS termination at LB + HTTP/1.1 -> HTTP/2 between LB and client could reslice frames and cause perceived backpressure.
- Client-side bug less likely (same repro with curl + node + browser), more likely network/proxy.

Things to try next (actionable):
- Get packet capture between proxy and runtime around the stall to see if data flows from runtime but proxy holds it.
- Reproduce with ALB in a controlled test and open AWS support ticket about ALB buffering for SSE.
- Add a small keepalive "comment" every 2s (":\n\n") to see if proxy reacts differently to heartbeat frames.
- Try HTTP/2 server push? (unlikely)
- Add explicit Transfer-Encoding: chunked + small chunk sizes from runtime lower than proxy threshold.
- Add an integration test in serving-runtime repo that spins up nginx with default config -> run sse_test and assert no stall; will help CI detect regressions.

Notes & informal thoughts:
- This doc is messy - quick capture while troubleshooting.
- Related GH issue: serving-runtime/issues/234 (linked above). Samir mentioned a similar problem in dedicated env around 2024-09 where a kube ingress had proxy-buffering on by default.

Next steps / TODOs: 
- [ ] Reproduce with packet capture (tcpdump) and attach pcap to GH issue.
- [ ] Add nginx fixture to tests and run nightly to catch regressions.
- [ ] If ALB is culprit, file infra ticket and consider switching those endpoints behind NLB (TCP) for streaming use cases.
- [ ] Share findings with infra and customer success for any impacted customers.

End of notes.
